finding_key: packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts::read-only enforcement is a sql keyword blocklist only; the newly added session `set` block omits `default_transaction_read_only`, so side-effecting functions inside a select can still write to the connected database
evidence: Verified against the supplied files: `executeQuery` (datasource.service.ts:143-145) issues only `SET statement_timeout`, `SET TimeZone`, `SET DateStyle` — there is no `default_transaction_read_only`/`SESSION CHARACTERISTICS ... READ ONLY`, and the only other gate is `validateSelectQuery` (sql-validator.ts:1-13), a whole-word blocklist of INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/etc. plus a "first token must be SELECT/WITH" check. So the claim's mechanics are accurate: `SELECT nextval('s')`, `SELECT some_volatile_writer()`, `SELECT pg_read_file(...)` contain no forbidden token, pass validation, and are executed inside the `SELECT * FROM (...) AS _q` wrapper; and the query endpoint only requires `assertMember` (datasource.controller.ts, executeQuery), so any workspace member can run it with the owner's stored credentials. Caveats on severity, not on truth: this gap is pre-existing (the PR only adds timezone/datestyle settings, it does not remove any read-only guard), it is explicitly acknowledged in docs/design/sheets/datasource.md's risk table ("function calls with side effects may still be possible. Consider using a read-only database role"), and exploitation depends on the configured connection user actually holding write/superuser rights on the remote DB.
